decisions.reason: F6 attributed finite additivity to monotonicity and a nonnegative restriction definition, neither of which states it. Added the existing nonnegative additivity corollary, signed/complex integral definition and L1 linearity theorem. Finite gluing gives Lp integrability before testing; overlap uniqueness and the finite grouped partition then give every weak derivative and both norm bounds. The Statement is unchanged.

False positive in the declared page interface: library/pde/weak-derivatives-and-sobolev-spaces.md explicitly indexes coordinates x_1,...,x_n and basis e_1,...,e_n; its examples page imports these conventions. Thus j=1,...,n labels canonical coordinate j-1, and the n summands include every first derivative. Checked the full argument: p-q(n-p)<0 controls scaled bumps; L=h^2 gives critical gradient bound h^(2-n), and the core and annulus function bounds are uniform. No undefined nth canonical coordinate is evaluated under this relabeling.

The owning A page declares x_1,...,x_n and e_1,...,e_n, and the examples page expressly adopts that convention. Hence x_n denotes the last coordinate (canonical index n-1), and j=1,...,n covers all n derivatives. The rejection ignores that relabeling. Independently checked bounded measurable gluing, nullity of the interface, normal-slice Newton-Leibniz using matching traces, tangential slices off the null parameter set, and completed-product Fubini. These establish the claimed derivative classes for both scalar fields and every p including 1 and infinity.

Step 3.3 uses the explicit owning-page convention x_1,...,x_n, imported by the examples page. Relabeling i by canonical i-1 includes every derivative exactly once, and |v|<=sqrt(n) max_i |v_i| gives the displayed bound for every p>=1. The coordinate objection is therefore false. Checked polar exponents n-1-ap and n-1-p(a+1), cutoff errors O(epsilon^(n-a-1)) with positive exponent in the sufficient range, locality/uniqueness for necessity, logarithmic divergence at equality, and essential unboundedness. No claim weakening or edit is needed.

The infinity witness lacks a value at j=0 under natural-number indexing. This is a nonfatal initial-index omission, repaired by replacing 1/j with 1/(j+1) and the error bound with (j+1)^(-1/4). Every approximant is smooth with bounded derivatives, converges uniformly to |x_k|^(1/2), and has zero i derivative for i distinct from k. The limit cannot be W1infinity because its k derivative is unbounded on positive-measure slabs. Checked the full/maximal graph limits using local weak stability and the finite-p jump witness using shrinking tensor tests. Statement unchanged.

Confirmed nonfatal choice-accounting defect: both Sobolev suppliers require Countable Choice, although the already assumed AC supplies it. F5 now retains that hypothesis, F6 explicitly restricts AC to countable families, step 1.2 discharges it, and step 3.1 distinguishes this use from HB. The mathematical reduction remains valid: the proved Sobolev norm gives a real or complex normed space and HB yields norm lower semicontinuity for weakly convergent sequences without completeness or reflexivity. Statement unchanged.

Confirmed nonfatal accounting error: the cited Lebesgue integration-by-parts lemma explicitly assumes Countable Choice, as do the first-weak-derivative and Sobolev interfaces. The item already assumes Countable Choice, so no hypothesis or claim change is needed. F4, F6 and step 4.1 now retain these uses. Checked both half-interval signs: each integral of |x| phi-second contributes phi(0). Injectivity on the two punctured halves forces any proposed regular representative to vanish a.e.; a bump equal to one at zero contradicts its pairing 2.

F7 improperly broadened a nonnegative integral definition; repaired it by explicitly extending restriction through positive/negative and real/imaginary parts and citing integral linearity. Also corrected the contradictory -(-1) typo in F5, specified j>=1 for the exhaustion, and supplied the existing indefinite-L1-integral AC and derivative theorems actually needed in F12/step 7.1. The full argument checks: summable local function/gradient errors give summable line increments; the one-dimensional sup bound yields uniform line convergence and an L1 derivative limit; the measurable Cauchy-set limit is one common ACL representative, identified with u and its weak derivatives by Fatou, subsequences and Fubini. Statement unchanged.

F3 incorrectly attributed the quotient to the measurable-function definition; F4 already supplied the exact quotient interface. Corrected F3 to describe only calligraphic Lp and refer the quotient assertion to F4. Checked the full composition proof: bounded F-prime gives a measurable Lp product independent of representatives, ACL on finite boxes gives the chain identity, the infinity case uses local W11 then essential bounds, and a test-dependent finite partition patches globally. The criterion F(u) in Lp and all three automatic cases remain intact. Also corrected the contract zero-input case: F(0), not necessarily zero, is the composite constant.

Confirmed a nonfatal coordinate-interface mismatch in F8: although the owning page labels coordinates 1,...,n, its literal e_i(i)=1 does not translate the cited vectors whose function domain is {0,...,n-1}. F8 now defines x_i=x(i-1) and e_i as canonical e_(i-1), making the n=1 calculation explicit without changing the Statement. Also corrected the false continuity claim for threshold indicators and the identification of a nonempty interface with an empty open degenerate box. Positive part followed by T_M yields exactly indicator(0<x_1<M)e_1; closed-box nullity justifies arbitrary interface values for every p.
